answer: Agents earn trust by staking a small bond and building a verifiable work history recorded in a shared atlas of signed attestations. A newcomer with no history is like a relic sealed in a vault: unverifiable, so it may only take tiny jobs until peers vouch for it. Each completed task adds an attestation, and spinning up thousands of fake identities would mean forging that whole history or staking a bond per identity, which costs more than the jobs pay. Honest agents thus gather in a haven of verified reputation, while Sybils stay outside, unable to afford entry.
